<properties>
{"title":"38. Spinor technology"}
</properties>
<content>
The four-component spinors $`u _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } )`$ and $`v _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } )`$ obey the equations
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#95ec5dd5d3cd491aa7219cdbdee94c8c">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { ( \rlap / p + m ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf p ) = 0 , } \\{ ( - \rlap / p + m ) v _ { s } ( \mathbf p ) = 0 . } \end{array} \tag{38.1}
	$$
</synced_block>
Each of these equations has two solutions, which we label via $`s = +`$ and $`s = -`$ . For $`m \neq 0`$ , we can go to the rest frame, $`\mathbf { p } = \mathbf { 0 }`$ . We will then distinguish the two solutions by the eigenvalue of the spin matrix
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#8ab36e5637f645adb4ac561422c76a7a">
	$$
	S _ { z } = { \textstyle \frac { i } { 4 } } [ \gamma ^ { 1 } , \gamma ^ { 2 } ] = { \textstyle \frac { i } { 2 } } \gamma ^ { 1 } \gamma ^ { 2 } = { \binom { { \textstyle \frac { 1 } { 2 } } \sigma _ { 3 } } { 0 } } \quad \ 0 \ \qquad \tag{38.2}
	$$
</synced_block>
Specifically, we will require
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#72fadba9c62f428d98abd17cb898db85">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { S _ { z } u _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \pm \frac { 1 } { 2 } u _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) \mathrm { ~ , ~ } } \\{ S _ { z } v _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \mp \frac { 1 } { 2 } v _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) \mathrm { ~ . ~ } } \end{array} \tag{38.3}
	$$
</synced_block>
The reason for the opposite sign for the $`v`$ spinor is that this choice results in
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#7f226cfa930045ffaa8c40aa11d66b5a">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { [ J _ { z } , b _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) ] = \pm \frac { 1 } { 2 } b _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) , } \\{ [ J _ { z } , d _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) ] = \pm \frac { 1 } { 2 } d _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) , } \end{array} \tag{38.4}
	$$
</synced_block>
where $`J _ { z }`$ is the $`z`$ component of the angular momentum operator. Eq. (38.4) implies that $`b _ { + } ^ { \dagger } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ and $`d _ { + } ^ { \dagger } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ each creates a particle with spin up along the $`z`$ axis. We will verify eq. (38.4) in problem 39.2.
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#1ac8273274f645d296516cae6564fa62">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { [ J _ { z } , b _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) ] = \pm \frac { 1 } { 2 } b _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) , } \\{ [ J _ { z } , d _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) ] = \pm \frac { 1 } { 2 } d _ { \pm } ^ { \dagger } ( { \bf 0 } ) , } \end{array} \tag{38.4}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
For $`\mathbf { p } = \mathbf { 0 }`$ , we have $`p \llap / = - m \gamma ^ { 0 }`$ , where
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#5fc065a574be44e989617404e0d58c31">
	$$
	\gamma ^ { 0 } = { \binom { 0 } { I } } \ \qquad \tag{38.5}
	$$
</synced_block>
Eqs. (38.1) and (38.3) are then easy to solve. Choosing (for later convenience) a specific normalization and phase for each of $`u _ { \pm } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ and $`{ \boldsymbol { v } } _ { \pm } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ , we get
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#2a20814e17d348a99e45e1630c5b0050">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { ( \rlap / p + m ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf p ) = 0 , } \\{ ( - \rlap / p + m ) v _ { s } ( \mathbf p ) = 0 . } \end{array} \tag{38.1}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#b2d3c7328008427283325c45aa2513a4">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { S _ { z } u _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \pm \frac { 1 } { 2 } u _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) \mathrm { ~ , ~ } } \\{ S _ { z } v _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \mp \frac { 1 } { 2 } v _ { \pm } ( { \bf 0 } ) \mathrm { ~ . ~ } } \end{array} \tag{38.3}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
$$
u _ { + } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( \begin{array} { l } { 1 } \\{ 0 } \\{ 1 } \\{ 0 } \end{array} \right) , \qquad u _ { - } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( \begin{array} { l } { 0 } \\{ 1 } \\{ 0 } \\{ 1 } \end{array} \right) ,
$$
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#c634db416f8e4c17a57956194db7759e">
	$$
	v _ { + } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( \begin{array} { c } { { 0 } } \\{ { 1 } } \\{ { 0 } } \\{ { - 1 } } \end{array} \right) , \qquad v _ { - } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( \begin{array} { c } { { - 1 } } \\{ { 0 } } \\{ { 1 } } \\{ { 0 } } \end{array} \right) . \tag{38.6}
	$$
</synced_block>
For later use we also compute the barred spinors
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#a53890a8d5024aa3afb34bf2ce376001">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { \overline { { u } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) \equiv u _ { s } ^ { \dagger } ( \mathbf { p } ) \beta , } \\{ \overline { { v } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) \equiv v _ { s } ^ { \dagger } ( \mathbf { p } ) \beta , } \end{array} \tag{38.7}
	$$
</synced_block>
where
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#8f8859bd76fd4efc9081dd5fd4c8ccb2">
	$$
	\beta = { \binom { 0 } { I } } \ { \binom { I } { 0 } } \tag{38.8}
	$$
</synced_block>
satisfies
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#5a7b12c1c500495aa656faf9bc05c892">
	$$
	\beta ^ { \mathrm { r } } = \beta ^ { \dagger } = \beta ^ { - 1 } = \beta . \tag{38.9}
	$$
</synced_block>
We get
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#076f9d0cd99d44fb86ab2cb1a3fb71a7">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r c l } { { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { + } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 1 , 0 , 1 , 0 \right) , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { - } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 0 , 1 , 0 , 1 \right) , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { + } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 0 , - 1 , 0 , 1 \right) , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { - } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 1 , 0 , - 1 , 0 \right) . } } \end{array} \tag{38.10}
	$$
</synced_block>
We can now find the spinors corresponding to an arbitrary three-momentum $`\mathbf { p }`$ by applying to $`u _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ and $`v _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ the matrix $`D ( \Lambda )`$ that corresponds to an appropriate boost. This is given by
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#55f552cc016f442380c6d269f29bacb8">
	$$
	{ \cal D } ( \Lambda ) = \exp ( i \eta \hat { { \bf p } } \cdot { \bf K } ) , \tag{38.11}
	$$
</synced_block>
where $`\hat { \bf p }`$ is a unit vector in the $`\mathbf { p }`$ direction, $`\begin{array} { r } { K ^ { j } = \frac { i } { 4 } [ \gamma ^ { j } , \gamma ^ { 0 } ] = \frac { i } { 2 } \gamma ^ { j } \gamma ^ { 0 } } \end{array}`$ is the boost matrix, and $`\eta \equiv \sinh ^ { - 1 } ( | \mathbf { p } | / m )`$ is the rapidity (see problem 2.9). Thus we have
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#f1493bab36db4b578eaeeb97822be073">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { u _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \exp ( i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } { \cdot } \mathbf { K } ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \ , } \\{ v _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \exp ( i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } { \cdot } \mathbf { K } ) v _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \ . } \end{array} \tag{38.12}
	$$
</synced_block>
We also have
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#665cb3401a884d89a59d6ce10a7128a3">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { \overline { { u } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \overline { { u } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \exp ( - i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } \cdot \mathbf { K } ) \mathrm { ~ , ~ } } \\{ \overline { { v } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \overline { { v } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \exp ( - i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } \cdot \mathbf { K } ) \mathrm { ~ . ~ } } \end{array} \tag{38.13}
	$$
</synced_block>
This follows from $`{ \overline { { K ^ { j } } } } = K ^ { j }`$ , where, for any general combination of gamma matrices,
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#b6dea56eed9042af90067ee78dee0822">
	$$
	\overline { { { A } } } \equiv \beta A ^ { \dagger } \beta . \tag{38.14}
	$$
</synced_block>
In particular, it turns out that
$$
\begin{array} { c } { { \overline { { { \gamma ^ { \mu } } } } = \gamma ^ { \mu } , } } \\{ { \overline { { { S ^ { \mu \nu } } } } = S ^ { \mu \nu } , } } \\{ { \overline { { { i \gamma _ { 5 } } } } = i \gamma _ { 5 } , } } \\{ { \overline { { { \gamma ^ { \mu } \gamma _ { 5 } } } } = \gamma ^ { \mu } \gamma _ { 5 } , } } \\{ { i \gamma _ { 5 } S ^ { \mu \nu } = i \gamma _ { 5 } S ^ { \mu \nu } . } } \end{array}
$$
The barred spinors satisfy the equations
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#f994a28a2d824a99ab4a3de86f4030f5">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { \overline { { u } } _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) ( p / + m ) = 0 , } \\{ \overline { { v } } _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) ( - p / + m ) = 0 . } \end{array} \tag{38.15-38.16}
	$$
</synced_block>
It is not very hard to work out $`u _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } )`$ and $`v _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } )`$ from eq. (38.12), but it is even easier to use various tricks that will sidestep any need for the explicit formulae. Consider, for example, $`\overline { { u } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( \mathbf { p } ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } )`$ ; from eqs. (38.12) and (38.13), we see that $`\overline { { u } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( \mathbf { p } ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \overline { { u } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ , and this is easy to compute from eqs. (38.6) and (38.10). We find
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#a8b9fc3ba0ba4835a8e3319774b7fa31">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { u _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \exp ( i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } { \cdot } \mathbf { K } ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \ , } \\{ v _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \exp ( i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } { \cdot } \mathbf { K } ) v _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \ . } \end{array} \tag{38.12}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#3eb6de9b49ff495ba29aa12a81276c17">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { \overline { { u } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \overline { { u } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \exp ( - i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } \cdot \mathbf { K } ) \mathrm { ~ , ~ } } \\{ \overline { { v } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { p } ) = \overline { { v } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) \exp ( - i \eta \hat { \mathbf { p } } \cdot \mathbf { K } ) \mathrm { ~ . ~ } } \end{array} \tag{38.13}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#cbc2ad42eda943d39f5f7308974d837c">
		$$
		v _ { + } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( \begin{array} { c } { { 0 } } \\{ { 1 } } \\{ { 0 } } \\{ { - 1 } } \end{array} \right) , \qquad v _ { - } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( \begin{array} { c } { { - 1 } } \\{ { 0 } } \\{ { 1 } } \\{ { 0 } } \end{array} \right) . \tag{38.6}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#0435a45cbcc54977b2bed6f19ee66001">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r c l } { { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { + } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 1 , 0 , 1 , 0 \right) , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { - } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 0 , 1 , 0 , 1 \right) , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { + } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 0 , - 1 , 0 , 1 \right) , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { - } ( { \bf 0 } ) = \sqrt { m } \left( 1 , 0 , - 1 , 0 \right) . } } \end{array} \tag{38.10}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#ca0f846a8cf244d08ddc3e207d709b3c">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r c l } { { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) u _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = + 2 m \delta _ { s ^ { \prime } s } ~ , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) v _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = - 2 m \delta _ { s ^ { \prime } s } ~ , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) v _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = 0 ~ , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) u _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = 0 ~ . } } \end{array} \tag{38.17}
	$$
</synced_block>
Also useful are the Gordon identities,
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#acb1b5c6f8604bc891a86ce1dacdcaf9">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { 2 m \overline { { u } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p ^ { \prime } } ) \gamma ^ { \mu } u _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = \overline { { u } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p ^ { \prime } } ) \Big [ ( p ^ { \prime } + p ) ^ { \mu } - 2 i S ^ { \mu \nu } ( p ^ { \prime } - p ) _ { \nu } \Big ] u _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) \ , } \\{ - 2 m \overline { { v } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p ^ { \prime } } ) \gamma ^ { \mu } v _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = \overline { { v } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p ^ { \prime } } ) \Big [ ( p ^ { \prime } + p ) ^ { \mu } - 2 i S ^ { \mu \nu } ( p ^ { \prime } - p ) _ { \nu } \Big ] v _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) \ . } \end{array} \tag{38.18}
	$$
</synced_block>
To derive them, start with
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#6c62f20351814938b9f1266c39b2d7ae">
	$$
	\begin{array} { c } { { \gamma ^ { \mu } p \llap / = \frac 1 2 \{ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / \} + \frac 1 2 [ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / ] = - p ^ { \mu } - 2 i S ^ { \mu \nu } p _ { \nu } ~ , } } \\{ { \nonumber } } \\{ { \gamma \llap / ^ { \prime } \gamma ^ { \mu } = \frac 1 2 \{ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / ^ { \prime } \} - \frac 1 2 [ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / ^ { \prime } ] = - p ^ { \prime \mu } + 2 i S ^ { \mu \nu } p _ { \nu } ^ { \prime } ~ . } } \end{array} \tag{38.19-38.20}
	$$
</synced_block>
Add eqs. (38.19) and (38.20), sandwich them between $`\overline { { u } } ^ { \prime }`$ and $`u`$ spinors (or $`\overline { { v } } ^ { \prime }`$ and $`v`$ spinors), and use eqs. (38.1) and (38.16). An important special case is $`p ^ { \prime } = p`$ ; then, using eq. (38.17), we find
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#87ee750b4fd04683bebf572b03fd4966">
		$$
		\begin{array} { c } { { \gamma ^ { \mu } p \llap / = \frac 1 2 \{ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / \} + \frac 1 2 [ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / ] = - p ^ { \mu } - 2 i S ^ { \mu \nu } p _ { \nu } ~ , } } \\{ { \nonumber } } \\{ { \gamma \llap / ^ { \prime } \gamma ^ { \mu } = \frac 1 2 \{ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / ^ { \prime } \} - \frac 1 2 [ \gamma ^ { \mu } , p \llap / ^ { \prime } ] = - p ^ { \prime \mu } + 2 i S ^ { \mu \nu } p _ { \nu } ^ { \prime } ~ . } } \end{array} \tag{38.19-38.20}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#6f018bc4b6024e6d837f6a5903cc2149">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { ( \rlap / p + m ) u _ { s } ( \mathbf p ) = 0 , } \\{ ( - \rlap / p + m ) v _ { s } ( \mathbf p ) = 0 . } \end{array} \tag{38.1}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#356f80317cf2491c8742a47663f5fc51">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { \overline { { u } } _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) ( p / + m ) = 0 , } \\{ \overline { { v } } _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) ( - p / + m ) = 0 . } \end{array} \tag{38.15-38.16}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#d1a6a3f4f1b54b0b81572f56ee8408c6">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r c l } { { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) u _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = + 2 m \delta _ { s ^ { \prime } s } ~ , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) v _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = - 2 m \delta _ { s ^ { \prime } s } ~ , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { u } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) v _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = 0 ~ , } } \\{ { } } & { { } } & { { \overline { { { v } } } _ { s ^ { \prime } } ( { \bf p } ) u _ { s } ( { \bf p } ) = 0 ~ . } } \end{array} \tag{38.17}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#82593cbb629d4e83bce6fdf00a45160e">
	$$

It is interesting to consider the extreme relativistic limit of this formula. Let us take the three-momentum to be in the $`z`$ direction, so that it is parallel to the spin-quantization axis. The component of the spin in the direction of the three-momentum is called the helicity. A fermion with helicity $`+ 1 / 2`$ is said to be right-handed, and a fermion with helicity $`- 1 / 2`$ is said to be left-handed. For rapidity $`\eta`$ , we have
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#b0ec5b210fcb4c4d9092e3faa5067359">
	$$

	$$
</synced_block>
The first equation is simply the definition of $`\eta`$ , and the second follows from $`z ^ { 2 } = 1`$ and $`p \cdot z = 0`$ (along with the knowledge that a boost of a four-vector in the $`z`$ direction does not change its $`x`$ and $`y`$ components). In the limit of large $`\eta`$ , we see that
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#d0bc64dc0c844501a8b413780da5354d">
	$$

	$$
</synced_block>

<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/19f10ddaf77242df946f54f8c3f99be6#7128354239c146619660358d29434b65">

The spinor corresponding to a right-handed fermion (helicity $`+ 1 / 2`$ ) is $`u _ { + } ( \mathbf { p } )`$ for a $`b`$ -type particle and $`v _ { - } ( \mathbf { p } )`$ for a $`d`$ -type particle. Similarly, left-handed fermions are projected (in the extreme relativistic limit) onto the upper two spinor components only, corresponding to the left-handed Weyl field.

(38.6), (38.10), and (38.33), we can show that $`\mathcal { C } \overline { { \mathscr { u } } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) ^ { \mathrm { r } } = v _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ and $`\mathcal { C } \overline { { \boldsymbol { v } } } _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } ) ^ { \mathrm { r } } = u _ { s } ( \mathbf { 0 } )`$ .
